050f94915a78630f57e70c7a98c2e9a80269f2ae.content:
{
"Heating and Cooling System": "The combined equipment in a building used to warm, cool, and circulate indoor air for occupant comfort. It typically includes heat generation, cooling, and air distribution components working together.",
"HVAC System": "A heating, ventilation, and air conditioning system that controls indoor temperature, humidity, and air quality. It integrates equipment such as furnaces, air conditioners, heat pumps, and ductwork.",
"Heat Pump": "An electrically powered device that transfers heat between indoors and outdoors to provide both heating and cooling. It uses a refrigerant cycle and can reverse direction seasonally.",
"Furnace": "A heating appliance that burns fuel or uses electricity to produce warm air, which is then distributed through ductwork. It is often paired with a central air conditioner or heat pump.",
"Central Air Conditioner": "A whole-house cooling system that uses a refrigerant cycle and ductwork to remove heat and moisture from indoor air. It consists of an indoor coil, outdoor unit, and compressor.",
"Backup Heat": "A secondary heating source that activates when the primary system, typically a heat pump, cannot meet demand. It ensures adequate warmth during very cold weather or deep setbacks.",
"Electric Backup Heat": "Resistance-based electric heating elements used as supplemental heat in a heat pump system. It consumes significantly more energy than the heat pump's normal operation.",
"Air Filter": "A replaceable component that traps dust and particles from air flowing through the HVAC system. It protects the equipment and improves indoor air quality.",
"Pleated Filter": "An air filter with a folded media design that provides increased surface area for capturing particles. It offers better filtration than flat filters without greatly restricting airflow.",
"MERV Rating": "The Minimum Efficiency Reporting Value, a standardized scale that measures how effectively an air filter captures airborne particles. Higher MERV values indicate finer filtration.",
"Blower": "The fan assembly inside an HVAC system that moves air through the coils and ductwork. It is driven by a motor and is essential for air distribution.",
"Blower Motor": "The electric motor that powers the blower fan in an HVAC system. Its performance affects airflow, efficiency, and system longevity.",
"Indoor Coil": "A heat-exchange coil located inside the air handler where refrigerant absorbs or releases heat to indoor air. It is also called the evaporator coil in cooling mode.",
"Outdoor Coil": "The heat-exchange coil located in the outdoor unit that releases or absorbs heat to or from outside air. It works with the indoor coil through the refrigerant cycle.",
"Compressor": "The pump in an HVAC system that pressurizes refrigerant and drives the refrigeration cycle. It is housed in the outdoor unit and is critical for heating and cooling.",
"Refrigerant": "A chemical fluid that cycles between liquid and gas states to transfer heat within an HVAC system. It is essential to the operation of heat pumps and air conditioners.",
"Refrigerant Charge": "The quantity of refrigerant contained in an HVAC system. Proper charge levels are required for efficient heating and cooling performance.",
"Condensate Drain": "A drain line that carries water condensed from indoor air at the cooling coil away from the air handler. If blocked, it can cause water damage and raise indoor humidity.",
"Air Handler": "The indoor component of an HVAC system that houses the blower, indoor coil, and filter. It circulates conditioned air through the ductwork.",
"Outdoor Unit": "The exterior cabinet of a heat pump or central air conditioner housing the compressor, outdoor coil, and fan. It exchanges heat with outside air.",
"Thermostat": "A control device that senses indoor temperature and signals the HVAC system to maintain a desired setpoint. It serves as the user interface for the heating and cooling system.",
"Programmable Thermostat": "A thermostat that allows users to schedule temperature setpoints at different times of day. It saves energy by automatically adjusting during sleep or away periods.",
"Setpoint": "The target indoor temperature that the thermostat is set to maintain. The HVAC system cycles on and off to keep the room near this value.",
"Setback": "A programmed reduction in the heating setpoint (or increase in the cooling setpoint) during periods when less conditioning is needed. Deep setbacks with heat pumps can trigger backup heat.",
"Indoor Humidity": "The amount of moisture in the air inside a building, usually expressed as relative humidity. HVAC systems help maintain healthy levels between 30 and 50 percent.",
"Ductwork": "The network of channels that distributes conditioned air throughout a building and returns it to the air handler. Its integrity directly affects efficiency and comfort.",
"Duct Insulation": "Thermal insulating material wrapped around ducts to reduce heat loss or gain, especially in unconditioned spaces. It improves HVAC efficiency and delivered air temperature.",
"Duct Sealing": "The process of closing leaks in ductwork joints and seams to prevent conditioned air loss. Common sealing materials include mastic and foil tape.",
"Mastic": "A thick, paint-like sealant applied to duct joints to create a durable, airtight seal. It is preferred over cloth duct tape for long-lasting duct sealing.",
"Foil Tape": "An adhesive metallic tape used to seal duct seams and joints. It is rated for HVAC use and withstands temperature changes better than cloth duct tape.",
"Unconditioned Space": "An area of a building, such as an attic or crawl space, that is not heated or cooled. Ducts and equipment in these areas require insulation to limit energy loss.",
"HVAC Contractor": "A licensed professional who installs, maintains, and repairs heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems. They perform tune-ups and diagnose system issues.",
"Tune-Up": "A scheduled maintenance visit by an HVAC contractor to inspect, clean, and adjust the system. It helps ensure efficient operation and extends equipment life.",
"Maintenance Task": "A specific action performed to keep HVAC equipment running reliably, such as changing filters or cleaning coils. Regular tasks prevent breakdowns and preserve efficiency.",
"Filter Change": "The replacement of a used air filter with a clean one. Doing this regularly maintains airflow and protects HVAC components from dust buildup.",
"Cooling Season": "The time of year, typically spring and summer, when the HVAC system is primarily used to cool the home. Air conditioners and heat pumps run most heavily during this period.",
"Heating Season": "The time of year, typically fall and winter, when the HVAC system is primarily used to warm the home. Furnaces and heat pumps run most heavily during this period.",
"Electrical Connection": "A point where wires join HVAC components to supply power or signals. Loose connections can cause high current draw and shorten equipment life.",
"Voltage": "The electrical potential difference supplied to HVAC components, measured in volts. Correct voltage is required for safe and efficient motor operation.",
"Current Draw": "The amount of electrical current, measured in amps, that a motor or component pulls during operation. Elevated current draw can indicate mechanical or electrical problems.",
"Lubrication": "The application of oil or grease to moving parts such as motor bearings to reduce friction and wear. It is part of routine HVAC maintenance.",
"System Controls": "The electronic and electromechanical devices that regulate HVAC startup, shutdown, and operating modes. They include thermostats, relays, and safety switches.",
"Starting Cycle": "The sequence of actions the HVAC system performs when it begins operating. Proper startup protects components and ensures efficient operation.",
"Shut-Off Sequence": "The ordered steps the HVAC system follows when it stops operating. A correct sequence prevents damage and completes any post-run tasks like fan runoff.",
"Defrost Cycle": "A mode in which a heat pump temporarily reverses operation to melt frost or ice from the outdoor coil. It is essential for maintaining efficiency in cold weather.",
"Airflow": "The volume and movement of air circulating through the HVAC system and ductwork. Adequate airflow is necessary for comfort, efficiency, and equipment protection.",
"Attic": "The space between a building's top-floor ceiling and its roof, often unconditioned. Ductwork or equipment located here should be sealed and insulated.",
"Crawl Space": "A shallow, unconditioned area beneath a building's first floor that provides access to plumbing and ductwork. Ducts in this space benefit from sealing and insulation."
}
